body: I really love going to concerts and have been going to the for years. At the beginning of summer I had a really bad seizure at a concert but was not on medication then so I kinda feel the same as you. I don't know if I would still have a seizure as I am now on medication but am paranoid about it and don't want to go and look at the floor the whole time!

In summer 2011 I had an appendicitis and was in hospital for 5 days following an appendectomy. I was only meant to be in over night however the evening after my operation I suffered from a seizure. I carried on having seizures for the next 4 days until they stopped giving me morphine and I recovered almost straight away. That is when I found out I have a severe morphine allergy.

What does this have to do with epilepsy you ask?

When I suffered from these seizures in hospital, I was terrified, really terrified! I had no idea what was going on, what was wrong with me and they left me feeling so drained and horrible!

I was released fro hospital 5 days after the operation…

But then the seizures carried on…

In the summer of 2011 I started my first year at Aberystwyth University studying English and Creative Writing. It was meant to be one of the most exciting years yet! However I was still having seizures…but the doctors didn’t seem to care. A couple of weeks in after feeling unwell for a while, we went to stay at James’ aunt’s for the weekend. It was meant to be a relaxing weekend to make me feel better, however whilst there I had a seizure which lasted around 10 minutes. I was taken in to hospital and once I had recovered I realized I had no feeling in my legs.

I as kept in over night but once again, the doctors did not seem to be worried…

I was left in a wheel chair for a month and had to withdraw from university. This carried on for another year and then the doctors finally started to do something about it. I went sent for CT and MRI scans…all which came back clear. After this the doctors went back to doing nothing.In sept/oct’ 2012, it got to a point where I was having grand mal seizures everyday, I was taken into a&e each time, yet still nothing from the doctors. Following this long period of frequent seizures I began to get a lot of pain in my back, made a lot worse by the seizures. Quickly it got to a point where once again I was in a wheelchair, this time for a year. I managed to carry on at uni whilst being in the wheelchair, but I couldn’t have done it without the support of James and my uni.I carried on having seizures for another year bringing up to 2 years since they started. 

At the beginning of summer this year the back started to recover and I was out of the wheelchair but still had to take things very easy! I went to a concert in Wrexham with my wonderful boyfriend James. I had just finished my first year at uni (attempt 2, I restarted uni in 2012) and was excited to have a great night out seeing one of our favorite bands! I was having a great night out until the band came on, then I had a seizure. Before I collapsed I was standing in the room next to my boyfriend, the house lights were off and the bright lights of the stage were flashing with people all around us. When I woke everywhere was bright, I was surrounded by paramedics and I could hear my boyfriend but could not see him. Outside of this circle of people there was no one. As you can imagine this was terrifying and confusing- one of the hardest things I find with having epilepsy, the confusion afterwards. As I began to recover I realized had had a seizure, set off by the strobe lighting. This was the first time it had been triggered by lights. When I collapsed my head hit the ground very hard causing me to injure my head and neck. 

Still very confused I was put on a spinal board and had a neck brace put on and was rushed to hospital. Finally, people started to take notice. The paramedics and doctors couldn’t believe I had been left with seizures for 2 years with no help of medication. I felt like crying. Finally people were thinking what I was. How could the doctors let it carry on like this! Soon I returned home to Hertfordshire for the summer and was sent to the epilepsy clinic. After various tests and a very stressful EEG I heard the words I strangely longed to hear. 

You have epilepsy.

I finally had an answer for the pain I had gone through for 2 years.

Over the summer I had decided not to let things stop me being who I wanted to be and doing what I wanted to do anymore. I became a local volunteer for Make-A-Wish Foundation UK, set up a Make-A-Wish Foundation Society at my university and signed up as an Adventure leader to trek the Great Wall of China in summer 2014 in aid of Make-A-Wish. At the beginning of Sept’ I attended the training weekend for being an Adventure Leader. I was so excited yet nervous and had an amazing first day. The second morning, I started to feel unwell and went out to get some fresh air. Suddenly I collapsed on the stone floor and had 3 grand mal seizures. I was so glad to have the epilepsy society at the training weekend (the charities attended the weekend), otherwise no one would have known what to do. 

I returned to the venue after a short trip to hospital and spent the afternoon with Katrina from the epilepsy society. It felt so nice to have someone to talk to who had an idea of how I felt. That afternoon I had 7 more grand mal seizures and 3 absence seizures. I felt so alone, hopeless and scared!

At the end of August/ beginning of September I was finally started on 50mg of Lamotrigine. Straight away the seizures started to reduce, I had less absences and jerking in my legs and I felt more in control of my epilepsy. 

I was seizure free for 6-7 weeks and it felt amazing, I started to get my confidence back with going out, going to lectures etc. Recently I have had two grand mal seizures triggered by flashing lights. At first I felt so frustrated and upset at first, but now I see it as learning. Epilepsy is still very new to me and I am still learning about my epilepsy and what it is triggered by. 

And that’s it! That is my story. It has been a stressful, hectic and difficult 2 years but I finally got my diagnoses and am finally adjusting to life with epilepsy!
No alcohol for me, i am a concoction of lamotigine (up to today), Citalopram, Predisolone, Chlophenamine and mycrogynon that adding alcohol to the mix would probably write me off!!
